title: Late-evening UTC two-hour window long in daily uptrend and high-volatility regime
rule_summary: Hourly candles, UTC. Regime is read from daily data at 00:00 UTC and holds for that whole UTC day. Uptrend: the last closed daily close is above the 50-day SMA of daily closes. High volatility: the 30-day standard deviation of hourly returns is above the median of that same measure over the previous 180 days (shortened from the source's 365 to fit the lab's lookback limit). ENTRY: on days when both hold, buy at the open of the 21:00 UTC hourly candle. EXIT: sell at the open of the 23:00 UTC candle (two hour hold, no stop). One position, whole balance, no other filters.
mechanism: The source offers no firm mechanism. The closest honest story: liquidity thins and US-evening order flow, plus retail and derivative-hedging flows near the daily roll, push prices up late in the UTC day; they pay for immediacy. The effect is likely strongest when volatility is high and the trend is up. Academic work finds time-of-day effects unstable across periods, and a 2-hour hold may not clear 0.35% costs.
